newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Storm turns HK activists back from disputed isles-radio.
newsitem.headline: Storm turns HK activists back from disputed isles-radio.

text.p: Bad weather and rough seas early on Thursday forced a Hong Kong protest ship to turn back from disputed East China Sea islands which they had hoped to reclaim from Japan, Taiwan radio said.
"Because of bad weather the ship has turned back," Taiwan state-funded radio said.

The broadcast, which gave few details, did not say whether a force of four Japanese frigates and a helicopter which tracked the vessel as it neared the islands late on Wednesday was a factor in the decision to turn back.

It was not known how close the civilian vessel, carrying 18 Hong Kong activists, 19 crew and 42 reporters, managed to get to the islands northeast of Taiwan, claimed by Japan as the Senkakus and by Taiwan and China as the Diaoyus.
Hong Kong radio and television had said the Japanese forces circled the rusty tanker Kien Hwa 2 several times while it was 60-90 miles (100-150 km) from the islands.

The ship had been due to arrive at the islands early on Thursday, with organisers pledging to go ashore to plant China's flag and remove Japanese flags and a lighthouse built in July by Japanese ultra-nationalists.
